investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-27T02:00Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint in us-east-2 was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at the POST /api/agents call before any evidence can be collected, all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning path — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)". This upstream failure prevented agent creation from starting, so no evidence was produced and the expected-output contract could not be satisfied. The failure is localized to the swarm gateway dependency of the remote-agents feature; no evidence of a broader production-api outage or user-traffic incident is present in the supplied packet.

possibleCauses: Swarm gateway ELB in us-east-2 was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run — the most strongly supported cause given the explicit 'bad_gateway' error and identical failure across all three sibling checks.

Transient network partition or DNS resolution failure between the production-api layer and the ELB endpoint, causing the connection attempt to fail before a response was received (latency of ~11 seconds across all three checks is consistent with a TCP timeout or connection refused scenario).
The ELB target group behind the swarm gateway had zero healthy instances (e.g., due to a deployment, scaling event, or health-check failure) causing the load balancer itself to return 502.

A misconfigured or rotated internal service credential/auth header required by the swarm gateway could cause it to reject requests, though the error message specifically says 'unreachable' and 'error sending request', which is more consistent with a connectivity failure than an auth rejection.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-27T02:00Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint in us-east-2 was unreachable during agent provisioning. investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning path — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)". The failure is localized to the swarm gateway dependency of the remote-agents feature; no evidence of a broader production-api outage or user-traffic incident is present in the supplied packet.

The ELB target group behind the swarm gateway had zero healthy instances (e.g., due to a deployment, scaling event, or health-check failure) causing the load balancer itself to return 502.
